comment: The table of std.rt. One row gives the copy of rt.buffer_append back to memcpy, whose ranges
must not overlap (ISO C11 7.24.2.1), where a module can give the bytes of the buffer itself. The
rows D12.2-rt-* hold the entries `regrow` and `regrow_move`: each test of `regrow`, the order of
its tests, the copy of the elements and the zero stores into the owner words of the old
elements. A std module is not part of the compiler binary, so the md5 guard reads the copy of
the module in the standard root of the debug preset, and the build copies it there itself. The
first stage runs run/stdlib/179, which links a memcpy that stops the run for overlapping ranges.
The second stage runs each program of test/lang whose name holds `regrow`: run/stdlib/180 to 184
call the two entries directly. The table runs in the VM with the default runner after `tools/vm

stages.name: the overlap test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc /usr/bin/clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu run/stdlib/179

stages.name: the regrow programs
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc /usr/bin/clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu -j 4 regrow

mutations.what: buffer_append copies with memcpy, which takes no overlapping ranges
a negative count is no error of its own
an unsigned count above the largest `i64` reads as negative
a count below the length passes
a count that equals the length is an error
a null pointer with a length that is not 0 passes
the size test comes before the length test
the operand test comes before the size test
the operand test comes after the storage
the new storage takes no element
an owner slot of an old element keeps its value
only the first owner slot of an element takes the zero value
only the first old element takes the zero stores
